title: Quantile spike dampener and region-aware soft-trip for dependency circuits
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Goal: Implement a region-aware, quantile-based 'spike dampener' layer for dependency circuit-breaking that reduces noisy trips from transient spikes while enabling conservative, deterministic fallback behavior for user-facing requests.

Motivation: Current per-dependency trips are sensitive to short high-percentile spikes (e.g. single-second latency blips during autoscaling churn). Those spikes produce noisy circuit flips and cascading fallbacks, increasing latency and instability for critical customers. We need a middle layer that smooths trips using quantile windows, token-weighted budgets, and regional damping so we only escalate to failover when we see sustained degradation or correlated failures across regions.

Scope:
- Introduce a Quantile Spike Dampener (QSD) that maintains short (30s), medium (5m), and long (1h) quantile summaries (p50/p95/p99) per dependency-model-region.
- Use a token-weighted error-budget: errors from large requests count proportionally higher for trip calculations.
- Dampening policy: require sustained q95 > threshold AND q99 spike persistence across short window before tripping.
- Region-aware hysteresis: prefer local throttling/soft-degrade first (reduced concurrency, shed low-priority tenants), then cross-region reroute only after two-region correlation.
- Shadow trips: QSD signals a "soft trip" to the routing layer without immediately blocking requests to collect canary metrics for 2 minutes before full enforcement.
- Safe fallback sequence documented and implemented: (1) local shedding (low-priority routes) (2) model-variant fallback (quantized/cheaper variant) (3) regional reroute (if peer healthy) (4) degrade to cached/approximate response or synthetic fallback.

Out-of-scope: full governance UI in Console (we will expose metrics and toggles but Console UX follow-up in separate ticket).
updates: 2026-02-18: Draft created by Miguel Santos. Initial hypothesis and metrics to track (q95/q99, token-weighted error rate, short/medium/long windows).

2026-02-22: Architecture spike complete. Verified we can compute streaming quantiles with existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus+stream aggregator). Implementation will add a lightweight in-runtime aggregator to avoid scrape latency for short windows.

2026-02-25: Design review with SRE and Product. Feedback: ensure soft-trip shadowing period defaults to 120s and provide override for high-traffic tenants. PM (Aisha Kapoor) requests opt-in per-tenant gate. Added as label.

2026-02-28: Prototype landed: in-runtime aggregator emits q95/q99 every 10s to local circuit controller. Token-weighted counting implemented (tokens multiplied by error flag). Observed decreased false-positive trips in canary run (canary: 3 services, 24h).
2026-03-01: Security/Compliance review: no plaintext sensitive data in dampener metrics, KMS/HSM not needed for these signals. SRE asked for rate-limited webhook to alert on soft-trip enter/exit.

2026-03-03: Rollout plan approved in sync: staged rollout - 5% of production traffic (internal beta), then 25% with telemetry checks, then 100%. Need to add runbook steps for manual rollback and forced disable per-region.

2026-03-03: Next actions assigned: Sofia to implement routing enforcement + shadow flag; Jonah Patel to add Console metrics and feature toggle (separate UI ticket); Miguel to write runbook and integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: QSD computes short/medium/long quantiles (p50/p95/p99) for target dependencies with <= 10s emit latency.
Soft-trip shadowing is implemented and produces telemetry events without blocking traffic for configured shadow window (default 120s).
Token-weighted error budget logic reduces false trips in canary by >= 60% compared to baseline for 95th+ percentile blips.
Routing layer enforces the documented fallback sequence when a full trip is activated, with per-region override in config.
Integration test coverage for simulated spike scenarios (transient blips, sustained degradation, cross-region correlated failures).
notes: Trade-offs: adding in-runtime quantile aggregation increases memory slightly (estimated +3% on edge routing pods) but reduces noisy circuit flips which reduce overall CPU from churn. We chose streaming GK quantile algorithm (t-digest variant) to balance accuracy and memory.
Review feedback: PM prefers conservative defaults; SRE prefers more aggressive regional failover for internal infra - we settled on policy flags per environment.
Follow-ups: UI ticket for Console controls (PM assigned Jonah Patel), a separate ticket to expose per-tenant opt-in and billing implications.
